subject: Hosted API: Legacy data deletion playbook & snapshot erase timeline
messages:
From: Tom Hargreaves <tom.hargreaves@lumenfinance.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@lumenfinance.com, Lumen Security <security@lumenfinance.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API: data retention & deletion Qs (legacy snapshots)

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this. We are finalizing our vendor security questionnaire for the Hosted API and have a handful of targeted questions around legacy backups and snapshot deletion. Please provide short, clear answers we can include in the RFP pack. Primary concerns are around copies of customer data that may live outside the active dataset (snapshots/backups, cold storage, cross-region replicas).

1) Do you maintain point-in-time snapshots/backups of Hosted API customer data? If yes, where (object store, internal block storage, etc.) and what is the retention period for those snapshots by default?
2) Are cross-region replicas created for HA/DR? If so, what regions are used and what is the retention and automatic deletion behavior for replicas?
3) What is the documented SLA for permanent deletion of data after a customer-initiated erase request? How long until backups/snapshots are scrubbed?
4) Can Redwood provide attestations/evidence that a snapshot was deleted (e.g., audit logs, snapshot ID, storage object deletion record)?
5) How do you handle short-lived caches (KV caches, inference prefix caches)? Are they persisted to durable storage at any point?
6) If we place a legal preservation/hold on an account, what is the mechanism and how long can retention hold be maintained?

If useful, we can take the answers as a spreadsheet (one column per question) and attach as part of the security deliverable.

Appreciate a response by Thursday if possible — procurement timeline is tight.

Cheers,
Tom
Tom Hargreaves
Head of Vendor Security, Lumen Finance
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hargreaves <tom.hargreaves@lumenfinance.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, Lumen Security <security@lumenfinance.com>, procurement@lumenfinance.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API: data retention & deletion Qs (legacy snapshots)

Tom — thanks for the clear list. I put together concise answers below and attached a short spreadsheet and a retention matrix for backup types (Lumen_SQ_v1.xlsx, snapshot-retention-matrix.pdf). Kimberly and Rishi — tagging for quick review / any phrasing tweaks.

--Answers (draft)--
1) Snapshots/backups: For the Hosted API we retain periodic service-level backups (object-store snapshots of model-serving state and customer-managed storage used for dataset ingestion) in our encrypted object store (AWS S3 for US regions, GCS for partner regions). By default snapshot retention is 90 days for standard service backups; customer-managed dataset exports are retained per the tenant's configured TTL or by request.

2) Cross-region replicas: We maintain cross-region replication strictly for high-availability (primary region + one warm replica in a paired region). Replicas are subject to the same retention policy (90 days) and are removed automatically when the corresponding snapshot/backup is scrubbed. Replica locations follow customer region selection (e.g., us-west <-> us-east).

3) Deletion SLA: For customer-initiated permanent deletion requests we remove live data within 48 hours and initiate backup/snapshot scrubbing within 30 days. Full cryptographic or object-level scrub of all long-lived backups occurs within 90 days from request completion. Exceptions: legal holds (see 6).

4) Evidence/attestation: We can provide deletion evidence that includes audit log entries, snapshot IDs, and object deletion records (storage object keys and timestamps). Evidence is provided as CSV/JSON and can be packaged in the security evidence folder (see Drive link).

5) Short-lived caches: Inference KV caches and prefix caches are ephemeral and kept in memory or local ephemeral NVMe for the duration of the inference session. They are not flushed to long-term object storage; caches are zeroed on instance recycle. Default retention is effectively minutes to hours depending on workload; no durable copies are kept.

6) Legal preservation/hold: Customers can request a preservation hold via the Redwood Console support workflow or an enterprise support ticket. Holds are implemented by disabling purge/eviction and marking the tenant for preserved storage; the preservation window can be sustained for up to 365 days (longer by agreement) while we maintain evidence and immutable snapshots.

Attached: Lumen_SQ_v1.xlsx (answers copy) and snapshot-retention-matrix.pdf.

Next step: Kim / Rishi, can you please review points 1–4 for accuracy and add any legal/ops caveats? Tom — if these look good I'll finalize and send as a packaged response with an offer to walk through in a 30-min call.

Best,

Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API: data retention & deletion Qs (legacy snapshots)

Stephanie — quick pass from security/ops and one suggested wording change for the external answers. Inline comments below (copied into the draft file as tracked changes).

- Q1 (snapshots): Confirm we keep two snapshot classes: "service control snapshots" (90-day default) and "long-term export snapshots" (customer-initiated exports kept per tenant TTL). Add sentence: "Service control snapshots are immutable for 7 days to protect against accidental deletes, after which they become eligible for scrub under retention policy."

- Q2 (replicas): Clarify: replicas are warm (not read-write), used for DR and are deleted during the same scrub window. Add example region pairings in the spreadsheet (us-west-2 <-> us-east-1).

- Q3 (deletion SLA): Ops suggests adjusting language to remove the word "cryptographic" (we may rotate keys, but key-rotation != proof of deletion). Recommend: "We remove live data within 48 hours and initiate automated backup scrub within 30 days; complete removal of backup objects is targeted within 90 days."

- Q4 (evidence): We can provide audit logs and object deletion records. Note: for object stores operated by cloud providers we can provide provider object-deletion events and our internal audit trail; we cannot produce low-level storage vendor internal logs. Propose adding: "Evidence package will include our audit log entries and corresponding cloud storage object delete events where available."

- Q5 (caches): Confirmed. Add explicit line: "Caches are never written to durable customer buckets by default."

- Q6 (legal hold): Add mechanism: "Redwood support creates a preservation ticket and attaches immutable retention markers; holds are managed via the console and formally logged in the customer's security evidence folder."

Rishi — anything to add on forensic extraction / extended holds?

Thanks,
Kimberly

Preservation beyond 365 days can be accommodated under a commercial addendum; add DPA amendment draft (DPA_amendment-draft.pdf) to the attachments. Also suggest that we explicitly call out that enclave logs used for debugging are truncated to 90 days by default and stored in an auditable log service.

-Rishi

Subject: Final: Hosted API legacy deletion playbook & evidence options

Tom — thanks for the patience. Attached are the finalized items we discussed: Lumen_SQ_v1.xlsx (Q/A formatted for your RFP), snapshot-retention-matrix.pdf (breaks down snapshot classes and timelines), and DPA_amendment-draft.pdf (commercial addendum language for extended preservation).

Summary (short):
- Default snapshot/backups: service-control snapshots retained 90 days; long-term customer exports follow tenant TTL.
- Replication: warm cross-region replicas (primary + one paired region) follow same retention and are scrubbed with the source snapshot.
- Deletion SLA: live-data removal within 48 hours; backup/snapshot scrub initiated within 30 days and completed within 90 days.
- Evidence: we will provide an evidence package containing Redwood audit log entries and cloud provider object-deletion events where available (CSV/JSON manifest).
- Caches: KV and prefix caches are ephemeral (minutes/hours) and are not persisted to durable storage.
- Legal hold: preservation tickets via support; holds can be maintained up to 365 days by default (longer by agreement).

Next steps: I can upload these to the security evidence Drive folder (link below) and if you want we'll schedule a 30-minute walkthrough. If the retention timelines look acceptable to procurement, we can also route the DPA amendment for signature (DocuSign link included in the Drive folder).
